newsitem.title: ITALY: Boy, 15, dies in Italian botulism case.
newsitem.headline: Boy, 15, dies in Italian botulism case.

text.p: A 15-year-old boy has died in Italy in a fatal case of botulism linked to contaminated mascarpone, a sweet desert cheese, health officials said on Monday.
Nicola Sagiomo died on Saturday after being admitted to hospital in Naples, southern Italy, with severe stomach cramps.
His younger brother and a friend were also seriously ill in hospital after the three boys had eaten home-made tiramisu, a popular Italian sponge desert prepared with mascarpone.
They are among at least seven cases of certified botulism that have arisen in the Naples area, the Calabria region on the toe of Italy and the central town of Siena.
All have been linked to a batch of mascarpone with a sell-by date of October 3. Tubs of the soft cheese, sold under the Parmalat, Giglio and Sol di Valle brands, have been withdrawn from stores.
Health Ministry undersecretary Bruno Viserta said the ministry was awaiting the results of laboratory analysis of the product to assess the extent of the contamination.
He told La Repubblica newspaper that "tests have confirmed the diagnosis of doctors" that the botulism was in the cheese.
Botulism is a severe form of food poisoning from foods that contain a toxin which can affect the central nervous system. In fatal cases, death is often caused by heart and lung failure.
The bacterium is most typically found in improperly preserved canned raw meat.
